The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: MetricsAbsent on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: No metrics received from io-shop since 2026-11-11T03:21:00Z {A1} - 6m {A2} with no sample, against a scrape interval of 15 {A3} seconds. The series stopped rather than crossing a threshold, so nothing here says whether the shop is well: these minutes have no readings to judge, not readings that look bad.
Alert raised: 2026-11-11T03:27:03Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-11T03:27:07Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule fires as soon as its condition holds. The alert came 3 minutes 33 seconds {beyond_accounted_for} later than the 2 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the metrics' stopping is measured to. The record does not show what took the rest.
No metrics were collected from 2026-11-11T03:21:00Z {metrics_stopped_at} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) until they resumed at 2026-11-11T03:27:45Z {metrics_resumed_at} (in the minute Argus acted in, so dated to its action), showing the service back to normal. That is 6 minutes 45 seconds {duration} the metrics did not cover, not a stretch the service is known to have spent in trouble.
Log lines read reach into it until 2026-11-11T03:26:00Z {logs_reach_until}: [G46bc], [Gbac1], [Gad41]. They are the service's own account of that stretch: what they report there is what is known of how it was doing, and up to then the service was seen through them. The logs were read up to 2026-11-11T03:26:00Z {log_reading_ended} - nothing after that was read.
How the service did over that stretch is said by the document itself, from your answer to logs_show_serving_as_before: say nothing of it anywhere else. Where the chain's first step says nobody using the service saw anything wrong, cite those log lines for it without saying what they show.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute {held}, until 2026-11-11T03:28:04Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
Error rate: not measured by the metrics - none were collected from when the metrics stopped until they resumed; the log lines that reach into that stretch, [G46bc], [Gbac1], [Gad41], are the service's own account of it, so do not say nothing was measured; what they show is said by the document itself, from your answer to logs_show_serving_as_before.
Customer loss: none - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all.

What Argus did, in order:

  - [T2] 2026-11-11T03:27:18Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up

  - [T5] 2026-11-11T03:27:29Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service's metrics - they stop after the minute at 03:20 {T5.2}, and nothing covers the minutes since
  - [T6] 2026-11-11T03:27:29Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 03:21 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-11T03:27:30Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-11T03:27:31Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 {T8.2} day 6 {T8.3} minutes 3 {T8.4} seconds before Nov 11 03:27:03 {T8.5}
  - [T9] 2026-11-11T03:27:32Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 2 {T9.2} production changes

  - [T13] 2026-11-11T03:27:38Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T13.2} replicas run revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020, deployed at 03:21:22 {T13.3}

  - [T15] 2026-11-11T03:27:39Z {T15.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T16] 2026-11-11T03:27:39Z {T16.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T16.3} hour before 03:27:39 {T16.4}

  - [T24] 2026-11-11T03:29:37Z {T24.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/546

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-10T23:21:22Z {P1.1} deploy e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 by kuki: deployed revision e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - [P2] 2026-11-11T03:21:22Z {P2.1} deploy 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 by kuki: deployed revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - Flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - before the metrics stopped: 9 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 7 {G46bc.2} minutes, 03:14–03:20 {G46bc.3}. After they stopped: 9 {G46bc.4} occurrences in 5 {G46bc.5} minutes, 03:22–03:26 {G46bc.6}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - before the metrics stopped: 6 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 7 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 03:14–03:20 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 1.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 0.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 03:15 {Gbac1.7}. After they stopped: 5 {Gbac1.8} occurrences in 5 {Gbac1.9} minutes, 03:22–03:26 {Gbac1.10}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.11} to 1.50% {Gbac1.12}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.13}, highest at 03:22 {Gbac1.14}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - before the metrics stopped: 1 {Gad41.1} occurrence in 1 {Gad41.2} minute, 03:18 {Gad41.3}. After they stopped: 1 {Gad41.4} occurrence in 1 {Gad41.5} minute, 03:21 {Gad41.6}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1, also C2] Candidates blaming the same move of deploy/values-production.yaml, each reading it as a different kind of failure - different accounts of what it did, not one cause counted twice - each in its own words:
      C1: The deploy of 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 at 2026-11-11T03:21:22Z {C1.1} changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml, metrics.portName from metrics to http-metrics. The metrics rows stop at 2026-11-11T03:20:00Z {C1.2}. The shop kept serving normally: logs across the gap show only the usual low-rate ClientDisconnected errors. What broke is the reporting, not the service. [monitoring-blind-spot, confidence 0.55 {C1.3}, confirmed]
      C2: The metrics port name was renamed from metrics to http-metrics on purpose in the 03:21:22Z {C1.4} deploy, and the scrape configuration still selects the old name. The scrape therefore finds no target and the series stops. [monitoring-configuration-drift, confidence 0.35 {C1.5}, confirmed, as tested for C1]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What each deployment it looked into changed:
  - [D1] Deployment of revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 to io-shop, compared against e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9 - the revision deployed before it.
      modified deploy/values-production.yaml
        @@ -43,7 +43,7 @@ autoscaling:
         # the only sign is that the series stops.
         metrics:
           port: 9090 {D1.1}
        -  portName: metrics
        +  portName: http-metrics
         
         # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
         #
  - A file [D1] does not list is as it was at the revision [D1] compares against.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault: deploy/values-production.yaml sets `metrics.portName: http-metrics` (changed in 9f4ad14). deploy/scrape.yaml, the ServiceMonitor, still picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`. Its own comment says it picks by name, that the two names must match, and that nothing checks this: a name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error. So when the rename went out, the shop kept serving, but Prometheus had nothing left to scrape.
      
      The fix: change `endpoints[0].port` in deploy/scrape.yaml to `http-metrics`, matching the value now in production. This keeps the deploy that renamed the port instead of reverting it. Rolling the values back to `metrics` without this change would just leave the same trap for the next rename.
      
      The test: tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py reads both files from the repository root. It takes `portName` from the `metrics:` block of values-production.yaml and every `port:` under `endpoints:` in scrape.yaml, and asserts that each endpoint's port equals portName. It uses plain text parsing, so it adds no YAML library dependency. Against the files as they stood before this change, it is written to fail (`metrics` vs `http-metrics`). It turns the agreement the comment says nothing enforces into something CI checks, so the next rename that changes only one file fails a test instead of breaking the metrics silently.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'. [F1] names revision 9f4ad14 and [D1] is that revision's own diff - say what it shows rather than ask for it to be checked.

What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired:
  - [S1] deploy/values-production.yaml at 9f4ad14
      # Deployment configuration for the io-shop account service, production.
      #
      # Rendered into the cluster as a ConfigMap and mounted into the pod, which is
      # why the service reads this file rather than being handed environment
      # variables: the values here are the deployment's, not the code's, and changing
      # one is a change to configuration that ships without the service being rebuilt.
      #
      # Owned by whoever runs the shop. Changes here go out the way any other change
      # goes out - reviewed, merged, and synced by the platform - and land without a
      # single line of io-shop's source being touched.
      
      replicas: 3 {S1.1}
      
      resources:
        memoryLimitMiB: 2048 {S1.2}
      
      # How the platform scales the shop.
      #
      # Rendered into a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, so `replicas` above is only where the
      # deployment starts: the controller decides the count from there, between the
      # floor and the ceiling here, aiming to keep each replica at the CPU target.
      #
      # `scaleDownStabilizationSeconds` is how far back the controller looks before it
      # believes a fall in load is real. Kubernetes defaults it to 300 {S1.3} - five minutes
      # of the highest recommendation it saw - because a controller acting on the
      # reading in front of it acts on a reading its own last action produced.
      autoscaling:
        minReplicas: 3 {S1.4}
        maxReplicas: 6 {S1.5}
        targetCpuPercent: 70 {S1.6}
        scaleDownStabilizationSeconds: 0 {S1.7}
      
      # How the platform finds the shop's metrics.
      #
      # The shop exposes its per-minute figures on this port, and the scrape config
      # selects the target by the port's *name* rather than its number - which is
      # what lets the number move without anything having to be re-pointed at it.
      #
      # The name is therefore load-bearing in a way the number is not. Nothing in the
      # shop reads it: the process serves the same endpoint whatever this says, and a
      # name nothing matches leaves a shop that is publishing perfectly well and a
      # scraper that has stopped collecting it. No request fails, no page slows, and
      # the only sign is that the series stops.
      metrics:
        port: 9090 {S1.8}
        portName: http-metrics
      
      # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
      #
      # The account page reads this cache before it works a shopper's spend figure
      # out, and recomputes when the cache has nothing or cannot be reached. So the
      # shop stays correct whatever is written here - it only stays *fast* while the
      # address is right.
      cache:
        host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
        port: 6380 {S1.9}
      

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Rolled back the deployment of io-shop
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
  - AI-3 (mitigate, open): Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand
PR #546 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P2].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The scrape configuration finds the shop's metrics target by the port's name, not its number, and the deploy renamed that port in deploy/values-production.yaml from metrics to http-metrics without changing the name deploy/scrape.yaml selects, which is still metrics. The selector then matched no port, and the scraper had nothing left to collect. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the label the monitoring system uses to find the shop's figures, and the monitoring setup most likely still looked for the old name, so it stopped collecting them.
still_at_risk: Any deploy that names the metrics port differently from the name the scrape configuration looks for, whether the same rename going out again or one of the two files changing without the other, would quietly stop the shop's metrics being collected again without raising any error.
symptom: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped being collected
causal_chain 1: No sign was seen that anyone using the shop had a problem. What was seen instead was that the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and no samples covered the minutes after they stopped. (cites AL1; T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The deploy of revision 9f4ad14 at {P2.1} changed one value in deploy/values-production.yaml: it renamed the metrics port from metrics to http-metrics and left the port number at {D1.1}. When read at {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas were running that revision. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed"; T13, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 2 ruled_out 1: The earlier deploy of revision e283ba3 at {P1.1}. Metrics were collected with it in place up to the minute at {T5.2}. Once the rollback put that revision back, the metrics could be read again. (cites T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; M1, under "Actions it took"; T21, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics target by the port's name and was still looking for metrics, so after the rename it matched no port and had nothing to collect. (cites S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired"; F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen that would catch the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml no longer matching the name the scrape configuration selects. The values file's own comment says nothing in the shop reads that name, and that a name nothing matches fails silently. A rename in one file could therefore ship without the other file changing.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch would have been caught before the deploy reached production, and the shop's metrics would not have stopped.
contributing_factors 2: The MetricsAbsent alert fired {beyond_accounted_for} later than its evaluation interval, the scraping allowance and the minute-level dating of the stop can explain. The record does not show what took the extra time.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The alert would have fired sooner, and the stretch when the shop's metrics went unwatched would have been shorter.
action_items 1: Add a pre-deploy CI check, applied to every service and not only io-shop, that fails any change where a scrape endpoint's port name matches none of the port names the deployment renders.
action_items 2: Find what delayed the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop by {beyond_accounted_for} beyond what its evaluation accounts for, and remove that delay.
action_items 3: Link MetricsAbsent on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: When MetricsAbsent fired on io-shop, nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to it.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
